inventory.source: Connected Notion private and shared sidebar page listings

inventory.limitations: Classification is title-based. Page body, attachments, comments, recency, and content-level evidence were not fetched for all 367 pages. Long source titles were captured up to 120 characters in the inventory.

architecture_sections.A: Formal backbone — definitions, constraints, invariants, objective and proof obligations
architecture_sections.B: Interface control documents — contracts, typed boundaries, bridge fields and ICDs
architecture_sections.C: Safety case — hazards, safety oracle, residual risk and assurance argument
architecture_sections.D: Compute & temporal architecture — execution substrate, latency, scheduling and runtime
architecture_sections.E: Instant / Kripke memory — state, event traces, identity, bitemporal record and retrieval
architecture_sections.F: Perception / prediction / planning / safety oracle — four-nucleus arrangement
architecture_sections.G: Operations — mission, deployment, runtime operations and bounded action
architecture_sections.H: Governance — authority, admissible grouping, arrangement and change control
architecture_sections.I: Development & assurance — implementation evidence, testing, verification and validation
architecture_sections.J: Stakeholder documents — research, portfolio, product and external communication

relevance_levels.core: Title indicates direct L5/autonomy/ORGANON/PCG/EPU architecture relevance.
relevance_levels.supporting: Title suggests a method, formalism, component, or evidence path that may support the L5 architecture.
relevance_levels.adjacent: Related technical or scientific work without demonstrated integration into L5.
relevance_levels.portfolio: Career, education, or commercial record rather than a technical architecture artifact.
relevance_levels.unresolved: Insufficient title-level evidence for a reliable relationship.

taxonomy.confidence: Confidence applies to title-based inference only; descriptive titles are more informative than generic or untitled pages.

vcs_design.snapshot_semantics: Every saved checkpoint contains the complete threads, nodes, edges, next IDs and UI state; it is not a delta-only record.
vcs_design.stream_semantics: Streams are orthogonal analytical workspaces for major project dynamics. Each has an independent workingState and headId.
vcs_design.historicity: All streams and checkpoints in this export are synthetic conceptual snapshots authored from the current page-title inventory and L5 reference context. They are not recovered historical saves or evidence of past project execution. All timestamps are the export-generation time; stage labels indicate a designed progression, not observed dates.
vcs_design.practical_limit: The Canvas source imposes no explicit numeric cap on streams or checkpoints, but browser memory, JSON size, and import time remain finite practical constraints.

optimization_contract.J: Pareto objective vector (maximize): page coverage; thematic separation; cross-stream state differentiation; traceability to Notion; importer-validity and recoverability.
optimization_contract.F: Canvas schema-compliant exports with 1–26 threads, at most 50 columns, unique node occupancy within each thread/column in every live/working/checkpoint snapshot, valid checkpoint ownership and head pointers.
hard_constraints: One node per thread/column cell per snapshot
Every checkpoint references an existing owner stream
Each stream headId references one of its checkpoints
All edge endpoints exist in each snapshot
optimization_contract.finite_budget: 24 streams × 4 full snapshots = 96 saved checkpoints; 367 page nodes plus 26 theme anchors per snapshot.
optimization_contract.certification: Structural feasibility is tested below. Global optimality over all possible Canvas exports is not proved.

assumed: A-J section mapping from the supplied L5 reference document

verified: Unique page IDs in the listed page inventory
Grid occupancy, checkpoint ownership, head references, and edge integrity for every generated snapshot
